rules.common: The normalized surname has rank 1000 or better in the 2010 Census surname table (the published Top 1,000).
rules.rare: The normalized surname is in the table (100 or more occurrences) but ranks below 1000.
rules.novel: The normalized surname is absent from the table (fewer than 100 occurrences in the 2010 Census).
rules.normalization: Unicode NFKD, combining marks removed, lowercase, only the letters a-z kept (so O'Brien and Al-Rashid become obrien and alrashid, as in the table).

rules.common: The surname is listed and held by at least 0.5% of the 2015 South Korean population (49,705,663 in the table note).
rules.rare: The surname is listed with a population share below 0.5%.
rules.novel: Not derivable: the transcription lists only part of the surnames in use, so absence from it proves nothing; no Korean case uses this band.
rules.normalization: The Hangul surname string exactly as listed (one or two syllables); no normalization.
